questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real shift from "operating" controls to "engineering" them?
options: Only using the GUI, never any form of scripting or Terraform
Capturing a control as versioned, reviewable configuration instead of a one-off manual change in a portal or console
Disabling all controls so there is nothing left to maintain
Making every change directly in production with no record of it
questions.explain: A control is a decision about how the organization is protected, and that decision belongs in a file in a repository, not a setting only one admin can reconstruct.

questions.q: What does the azuread_conditional_access_policy Terraform resource let you do?
options: Delete a user's MFA registration automatically
Run only inside the Azure portal, never from a command line
Define a Conditional Access policy's name, state, and grant controls as plain-text configuration
Replace Azure AD entirely with a different identity provider
questions.explain: The Terraform resource expresses the policy declaratively, so it can be read, diffed, and reviewed like any other code.

questions.q: Why does putting a Conditional Access policy change in a pull request matter?
options: A second person reviews the diff and can catch a missing role or scope before the policy is enabled
It has no effect — Conditional Access policies can't be stored as files
Pull requests automatically enable the policy without any admin action
It replaces the need for the policy to actually be tested
questions.explain: In the lesson's example, a reviewer catches that Privileged Role Administrator was missing from the targeted roles before the change merges.

questions.q: What does Backup-GPO do, and how does Import-GPO use its result?
options: Backup-GPO only works on Azure AD Conditional Access policies, not GPOs
Import-GPO creates a brand-new, empty GPO with default settings
Backup-GPO snapshots every setting in a GPO; Import-GPO restores that exact snapshot by its backup ID
Backup-GPO deletes a GPO permanently with no way to recover it
questions.explain: Backup-GPO saves a point-in-time snapshot of a GPO's settings; Import-GPO restores that specific snapshot back onto the GPO using its backup ID, giving you a real rollback.

questions.q: Why isn't writing a control as code, by itself, enough to trust it?
options: Capturing a control as code doesn't prove the control works correctly once it's actually live — it still needs to be tested before broad deployment
Writing code always guarantees the control is correct
Once a control is written as code, it no longer needs a rollback plan
Code-based controls can't be reviewed by a second person
questions.explain: The lesson closes by pointing to the next step: testing in audit or report-only mode and rolling out to a pilot group, because defining a control isn't the same as validating it.
